data.title: Textbook:A Gift of Fire, Social, Legal, and Ethical Issues for Computing 62 Pearson Publishing by Sara Baase & Timothy M. Henry ISBN 13:978-0-13-461527-1

Course Description Professional and ethical responsibilities of computer scientists and software engineers as influenced by growth in computer use and networks. Costs and benefits of computer technology. Risks and liabilities of safety-critical systems. Social implications of the Internet. Interaction between human values and technical decisions involving computing. Intellectual Property. Global impact of computing. Dangers of AI and Robots. The Singularity. Topics will vary by class and level of participation. This course involves considerable reading, not just of the textbook but papers, as well. Don't get behind in the reading, since we will have homeworks on each reading assignment, and late assignments lose credit quickly. However, most of the reading is interesting and thought-provoking, so it isn't terribly difficult, and it would be helpful if you do it before coming to class. Grading will consider how well you explain and defend an opinion, not the opinion itself. That is, I don't care which side of an argument you take as long as you then explain and defend that side well. Please check your grammar and spelling, since while this is not directly graded, sloppiness that makes your writing difficult to understand can lose you a few points. Homework will be checked with Turnitin. Papers generated by ChatGPT will likely be detected, and I will apply University rules on cheating. If you don't do your own work you're not learning. When handing in work through Canvas, it is your responsibility to make sure it has been submitted correctly. Requests for a grade change after the late work deadline will not be considered. If the grader sees, for example, that you have handed in the assignment for another class you will get a zero for that assignment. Perhaps you have the correct assignment with timestamps showing you did it on time. Those don't count; your professor has written code that changes timestamps. See the syllabus for complete information. I will handle requests for special circumstances, such as illness, personal problems, etc. in person only. E-mail me to make an appointment and I will meet you even if you cannot come to my normal offfice hours. If your situation requires documentation, bring a paper copy with you. Let me know as soon as possible, not the final week of class. I would love for this to be an interactive class with lots of discussion, but considering that there are 150 students packed into the classroom, this is difficult. However, since attendance is usually spotty, if you sit near the front we can have at least some interaction. You are expected to read the material and attend classes, but attendance does not figure into your grade. I will pass around an attendance sheet for administrative purposes only; under certain circumstances I need to document to the registrar who was in class.

Learning Outcomes Ability to understand professional issues and responsibilities Ability to understand ethical issues and responsibilities Ability to understand legal issues and responsibilities Ability to understand security issues and responsibilities Ability to understand social issues and responsibilities Ability to analyze the local impact of computing Ability to analyze the global impact of computing

Format of Assignments Assignments must be handed in through Canvas. Here are the rules: Make a copy of the assignment document. Do not delete the description of what you are to do. Put your name and NetID in the assignment. Missing this is -5 points. Giving only your answer without the problem description is -10 points. Allowable formats are PDF and docx. Anything else will result in the loss of at least 20 points. Allowable fonts are any sans serif, such as Arial or Calibri Body. Size is 11 points Leave one blank line between paragraphs. Unless otherwise specified, write no more than to the bottom of the page, including references, if any Do not repeat the question in your answer; it is right there. Keep your writing short and to the point. There is no specific word count.
